newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish grain prices to stay flat in Q3 - ministry.
newsitem.headline: Polish grain prices to stay flat in Q3 - ministry.

text.p: Average Polish wheat prices are likely to stay flat in the third quarter and rye prices are expected to ease slightly, the agriculture ministry said in a Monday statement.
It said average wheat prices in the period would be 50-52 zlotys per quintal and rye prices 38-40 zlotys. In May, wheat stood at 51.18 zlotys per quintal and rye at 40.13 zlotys.

The ministry estimated that Poland would have grain reserves of 4.0 to 4.5 million tonnes in mid-1997, stocked by farmers, processing firms, traders and in state reserves. No comparative figures were available.
The statement said Poland's grain production, imports and reserves in the 1997/1998 season as a whole were expected to fall by 1.5 million tonnes from the 24.7 million tonnes of 1996/97.
Domestic consumption next year would rise 0.6 million to 26.2 million, it said. It did not say how the increased demand would be met.
Polish agriculture minister Jaroslaw Kalinowski told a news conference on Monday the government had currently no intention of lifting the 20 percent import duty on grains.
He said the current 15 percent rapeseed tariffs were likely to be lowered when the harvest was finished because expected output would meet only 50 percent of domestic demand.
Rapeseed output is seen at 400,000-450,000 tonnes this year, down from 500,000 tonnes in 1996 after an unfavourable winter.

"We are aware that the Polish industry's demand for rapeseed will only be met in 50 percent but only after it buys up domestic production, if it is necessary, shall we ask for import quotas with lower duties," Kalinowski said.
